about: Free assessment tools shown at the top of the Assessment page. Every field is plain text. kind is a list drawn from Screening, Diagnostic, Progress monitoring and Questionnaire. Only list a tool when its free access has been checked on the publisher's own site, and say exactly what is free. Describe each tool in the publisher's own terms: 'tells' is what the publisher says it measures and 'who' is the publisher's stated purpose. Do not add interpretation.

tools.name: DIBELS 8th Edition: Australasian version
tools.delivery: One-to-one for five of the six measures. Maze can be given to a group.
tools.time: One minute each for five of the six measures. Maze takes three minutes.
tools.tells: A set of short fluency measures for assessing the acquisition of literacy skills, namely letter naming fluency, phonemic segmentation fluency, nonsense word fluency, word reading fluency, oral reading fluency and Maze. For dyslexia screening, the subtests measure processing speed, phonological awareness and the alphabetic principle.
tools.who: Universal screening, benchmark assessment and progress monitoring. The publisher describes it as a way to regularly detect risk and monitor the development of early literacy and early reading skills.
tools.access: Free download
tools.note: This is the version adapted for Australia and New Zealand. Use it in place of the American materials.

tools.name: Year 1 Phonics Check
tools.by: Australian Government, on the Literacy Hub
tools.years: Year 1 (usually Term 3), Year 2 and older struggling readers
tools.tells: Students' decoding skills across words of increasing complexity, using real words and pseudowords. Students are categorised as fluent decoders (28 to 40), developing decoders (20 to 27) or struggling decoders (0 to 19).
tools.who: Identifying decoding strengths and instructional needs for individual students, classes and year levels, identifying students who might need phonics intervention, and tracking the effectiveness of phonics instruction over time.
tools.access: Free with a teacher sign-in
tools.note: Designed for students who have had at least 18 months of systematic synthetic phonics teaching.

tools.name: Year 1 Number Check
tools.by: Australian Government, on the Mathematics Hub
tools.delivery: One-to-one interview, online or on paper
tools.time: Not stated. Choose the 20-item check or the shorter 12-item check.
tools.tells: Whether students are developing the number and counting knowledge expected in Year 1. The 20-item check covers numeral identification, number sequences, skip counting, subitising, counting, addition and subtraction (including partitioning and flexible strategies) and multiplicative thinking.
tools.who: Checking progress and planning early intervention for children who may not yet be at the expected level of development. It is not compulsory.
tools.access: Free with a teacher sign-in
tools.note: Aligned to the Australian Curriculum: Mathematics Version 9.

tools.name: CC2: Castles and Coltheart Test 2
tools.by: MOTIf, Macquarie University (Anne Castles and colleagues)
tools.years: Ages 6 to 11 and a half (Australian norms)
tools.time: Not stated. Up to 120 words, stopping after five errors in a row of each type.
tools.tells: The key processes in single-word reading, namely sounding-out ability, assessed by accuracy reading nonwords aloud, and whole-word recognition ability, assessed by accuracy reading irregular words aloud. It has 40 regular words, 40 irregular words and 40 nonwords, presented one at a time in mixed order with increasing difficulty.
tools.who: Comparing a child's accuracy on each item type with norms from over 1000 Australian children aged 6 years 0 months to 11 years 6 months (the online version converts scores to z scores).
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details). A paid digital version is also available.

tools.name: LeST: Letter Sound Test
tools.time: Not stated. 51 single letters and letter combinations.
tools.tells: A person's ability to sound out single letters and letter combinations in isolation, not in the context of a word or nonword. It is a reading aloud task with 51 graphemes.
tools.who: Giving the tester an overview of which graphemes a reader can sound out, so the letter-sound correspondences not yet known can be trained.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details). A paid digital version is also available.

tools.name: DiRT: Diagnostic Reading Test for Nonwords
tools.tells: Knowledge of letter-sound correspondences at the word level. Its 105 nonwords assess over 60 letter-sound rules. Where the CC2 assesses whether a person has difficulty reading nonwords in general, the DiRT assesses which particular rules they can apply.
tools.who: An error analysis showing which letter-sound rules the reader knows, so the rules not yet known can be trained.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details)

tools.name: LIDT: Letter Identification Test
tools.tells: Letter identification knowledge, that is, which letter identities a person knows (for example, that d and D are the same letter). It is a matching task with 29 items.
tools.who: Giving the tester an overview of the reader's ability to match upper and lower case letters, so letter identification can be trained if needed.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details)

tools.name: LetPos: Letter Position Test
tools.tells: Children's ability to assign positions to letters in words. It uses 60 migratable words, in which the letters can be rearranged to make another word (pirates and parties).
tools.who: All children, and particularly screening for letter position dyslexia, where children make migration or anagram errors such as reading slime as smile.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details)

tools.name: TOC: Test of Orthographic Choice
tools.years: Compared with students in the same year level
tools.time: Not stated. 30 items and two practice items.
tools.tells: Written word recognition. The reader sees two written items that sound the same (doar and door) and chooses the one spelled correctly, which cannot be done by sounding out. 30 test items and two practice items.
tools.who: Comparing a reader's written word recognition with others in the same year level, who have had similar amounts of reading instruction.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details)

tools.name: TERC: Test of Everyday Reading Comprehension
tools.by: MOTIf, Macquarie University (Genevieve McArthur and colleagues)
tools.time: Not stated. 10 items of increasing difficulty.
tools.tells: How well a person understands what they read in everyday life, such as a canteen menu or the instructions on a medicine bottle. Ten items increase in difficulty, each followed by a question.
tools.who: A results page showing an overall score and a list of the everyday reading tasks the reader can and cannot do.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details). A paid digital version is also available.

tools.name: DiSTs: Diagnostic Spelling Test for Sounds
tools.tells: Whether a person can represent frequently occurring English sounds with the appropriate letter or letters, that is, the process of translating single sounds into letters. The tester says 32 sounds and the speller writes the letters.
tools.who: Showing which sounds the speller can represent in isolation, so the sounds not yet represented accurately can be trained.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details). A paid digital version is also available.

tools.name: DiSTn: Diagnostic Spelling Test for Nonwords
tools.tells: Knowledge of English sound-letter rules at the word level. The speller writes 74 dictated nonwords, which assess over 40 sound-letter rules.
tools.who: A detailed analysis of which sound-letter rules the speller can apply, so the rules not yet known can be trained.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details)

tools.name: DiSTi: Diagnostic Spelling Test for Irregular Words
tools.tells: Knowledge of whole-word spellings, tested with 74 dictated irregular words, which cannot be spelled correctly by following sound-letter rules and so must be learned as whole words.
tools.who: Comparing a student's irregular word spelling accuracy with that of children in Years 1 to 7.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details). A paid digital version is also available.

tools.name: DiST-m: Diagnostic Spelling Test for Morphology
tools.years: From around Year 3 through secondary school
tools.tells: The ability to apply morphological regularities in spelling, including some of the most commonly used suffixes (such as past tense -ed) and very consistent morphologically based spelling rules. It is a spelling-to-dictation test of 28 morphologically complex nonwords.
tools.who: Determining which morphological spellings to focus on in classroom teaching and intervention. There are no published norms; an error analysis shows which regularities have been acquired.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details)

tools.name: MAAST: Macquarie Advanced Adult Spelling Test
tools.tells: How well adults can spell difficult words that are commonly misspelled because they contain irregular sound-spelling rules. 72 dictated items.
tools.who: Assessing adult spelling. The publisher states no further purpose.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details)
tools.note: Made for adults, so it is not a school assessment. It is listed to complete the MOTIf suite.

tools.name: RAT: Reading Anxiety Tests
tools.delivery: Questionnaire, completed by the student or a parent
tools.tells: Questionnaires designed to detect elevated levels of anxiety related to reading. There are five, namely self-report and parent-report forms for children and for adolescents, and a form for adults.
tools.who: Detecting elevated reading anxiety in children, adolescents and adults.
tools.access: Free PDFs to print. The parent report for children also has a digital version.

tools.name: NeST: negative evaluations about reading
tools.delivery: Questionnaire, with child, parent and teacher versions
tools.tells: Whether a primary-school child feels they have received negative evaluations about their reading from significant others (peers, teachers, parents). There are child, parent and teacher report versions.
tools.who: Insight into a child's own perceptions of negative feedback about their reading, and who it comes from. There are currently no norms.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details)

tools.name: Australian norms for the TOWRE
tools.delivery: Used with the Test of Word Reading Efficiency
tools.tells: Approximate age-based and grade-based norms for Australian primary school children on the TOWRE (Test of Word Reading Efficiency), a measure of word reading speed. The data were collected in 2010 for the 1999 version of the test.
tools.who: Comparing a child's TOWRE performance with an Australian norm group, most reliably in the second half of the school year.
tools.access: Free PDF of the norms. The TOWRE itself is sold separately.
tools.note: The norms are for the original 1999 TOWRE, not TOWRE-2.

tools.name: BAPPA-F and BAPPA-R: plural processing in aphasia
tools.tells: The ability of people with aphasia to produce plurals, and the effects of word frequency (BAPPA-F) and regularity (BAPPA-R) on that ability, each across four tasks.
tools.who: Identifying whether processing of plural inflection is intact or impaired, and the level of the language system where the impairment arises. These are not school assessments and are listed so the suite is complete.
tools.access: Free PDF to print (you give a few details)
tools.note: Made for adults, so it is not a school assessment. It is listed to complete the MOTIf suite.

tools.name: Acadience Reading K-6
tools.years: Foundation to Year 6 (American Kindergarten to Grade 6)
tools.delivery: Not stated on the fact sheet. Oral Reading Fluency passages are read aloud for 1 minute; Maze is read silently.
tools.tells: The acquisition of early literacy and reading skills through six brief measures, namely First Sound Fluency (phonemic awareness), Letter Naming Fluency, Phoneme Segmentation Fluency (phonemic awareness), Nonsense Word Fluency (the alphabetic principle and basic phonics), Oral Reading Fluency with Retell (advanced phonics, word attack and reading connected text) and Maze (reading comprehension).
tools.who: Universal screening, with research-based benchmarks for all measures and grades, to monitor the development of early literacy skills, provide timely instructional support and prevent later reading difficulties.
tools.access: Free download from the Acadience Resource Hub after you register an email address. The online data system is paid.

tools.name: Acadience Math
tools.years: Foundation to Year 6 (American Kindergarten to Grade 6)
tools.tells: Early numeracy, computation and problem solving through seven measures, namely Beginning Quantity Discrimination, Number Identification Fluency (naming the numerals 1 to 99), Next Number Fluency, Advanced Quantity Discrimination, Missing Number Fluency, Computation, and Concepts and Applications.
tools.who: Universal screening designed to predict early mathematics success and identify students experiencing difficulty in acquiring foundational maths skills, and to detect the effects of intervention.
tools.access: Free download from the Acadience Resource Hub after you register an email address. The online data system is paid.
tools.note: Aligned to American standards, so check the fit with your scope and sequence.

tools.name: Acadience RAN and Acadience Spelling
tools.years: Foundation and Year 1 (American Kindergarten and Grade 1)
tools.delivery: Not stated on the overview pages
tools.time: Not stated on the overview pages
tools.tells: Acadience RAN assesses quick and accurate naming of repeated sets of familiar items. Acadience Spelling is a measure for Kindergarten and Grade 1 that the publisher says may be particularly useful where spelling is required as part of screening for reading difficulties such as dyslexia.
tools.who: Adding rapid naming and spelling measures to Acadience Reading K-6 screening in the first two years of school.
tools.access: Free download from the Acadience downloads pages. Other Acadience tools (Reading 7-8 and the Reading Diagnostic) are sold through the publisher Voyager Sopris, so they are not listed here.

tools.name: CUBED-3
tools.focus: Oral language, decoding and reading comprehension
tools.years: Not stated on the download page
tools.tells: The dimensions of literacy, namely language, decoding and their product, reading comprehension. The Narrative Language Measures (NLM Listening and NLM Reading) measure the ability to comprehend and produce complex, academic language. The Dynamic Decoding Measures have four subtests: Phonemic Awareness, Phoneme Manipulation, Orthographic Mapping and Decoding Inventory.
tools.who: Screening these skills in under five minutes, then gathering further data to identify specific weaknesses in language or decoding to inform instruction.
tools.access: Free paper and pencil version to download for personal use after you give a name and email address. The digital version is paid.

tools.name: PAST: Phonological Awareness Screening Test
tools.tells: Phonemic awareness and phonemic proficiency, which the author defines as automatic, unconscious access to the phonemes in spoken words. Items run from syllable level to phoneme level.
tools.who: Assessing students a few times a year to track progress, using the four forms (A to D). The author asks that testers study the instructions carefully before giving it.
tools.access: Free download (four forms, with instructions)
